messages.author: fa8b9dad524607ca
messages.subject: Help with... 'help'
parts:
Greetings shiners,

Right now my app is nearly complete, but I noticed it is devoid of 'help' functionality.  Initially I suggested to a colleague that I have a checkbox for 'show instructions' to go along with each tab, displaying text in the main panel for telling the user what to do in each section.  However, she had an interesting idea, but I am not sure if it is beyond the capabilities of shiny at the moment or not.  She suggested that there be a help icon '?', which when moused over, would show the instructions for each section.  Currently, it appears that the mouse over text is simply the name of the tab which is currently selected, wherever it currently is.  Any suggestions on how to accomplish this, or other ways to supply help/instructions in an aesthetically pleasing manner, would all be very much appreciated.

Thanks,
Mike

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Help with... 'help'
parts:
Try slapping this at the top of ui.R:

helpPopup <- function(title, content,
                      placement=c('right', 'top', 'left', 'bottom'),
                      trigger=c('click', 'hover', 'focus', 'manual')) {
  tagList(
    singleton(
      tags$head(
        tags$script("$(\"[data-toggle='popover']\").popover()")
      )
    ),
    tags$a(
      href = "#", class = "btn btn-mini", `data-toggle` = "popover",
      title = title, `data-content` = content, `data-animation` = TRUE,
      `data-placement` = match.arg(placement, several.ok=TRUE)[1],
      `data-trigger` = match.arg(trigger, several.ok=TRUE)[1],
      
      tags$i(class="icon-question-sign")
    )
  )
}

Then sprinkle helpPopup calls liberally throughout your app :)

messages.subject: Re: Help with... 'help'
parts:
Nope. Don't think it is possible. It does work in a bootstrap modal however. Try this:

helpModal <- function(title, link, content) {
  html <- sprintf("<div id='%s' class='modal hide fade in' style='display: none; '>
                     <div class='modal-header'><a class='close' data-dismiss='modal' href='#'>×</a>
                       <h3>%s</h3>
                     </div>
                     <div class='modal-body'>%s</div>
                   </div>
                   <a title='Help' data-toggle='modal' href='#%s' class='icon-question-sign'></a>", link, title, content, link)
  Encoding(html) <- 'UTF-8'
  HTML(html)
}

where you pass html generated by includeMarkdown or from a processed Rmd file with math. You may want this in your css file:

.modal { 
  width: 800px; 
  left: 600px; 
}

.modal-body {
  height: 100%;
  max-height:500px;
}

To get math to work with knitr for 'reporting' in my app:

        return(HTML(paste(knit2html(text = input$rmd_report, fragment.only = TRUE, quiet = TRUE), '<script>', 'MathJax.Hub.Typeset();', '</script>', sep = '\n')))

Where input$rmd_report is the content of shinyAce

messages.subject: Re: Help with... 'help'
parts:
You can test the current development version on Github -- the function
includeMathJax() is a wrapper of tags$script(src =
"...mathjax-src..."). MathJax expressions will work with
uiOutput()/renderUI(), but popovers are a very special case, because
the content of a pop over is stored in a character string when the
HTML document is loaded, then MathJax won't see it since it is not
part of the DOM. Modals work because the content is stored in a hidden
div (i.e. "display: hide"), and MathJax can recognize math expressions
even when they are hidden.

To Stéphane: I do not think it is easy to get popovers work with
MathJax. You can certainly aggressively call MathJax.Hub.Typeset() in
the page but that does not sound like a good idea:

tags$script(HTML("setInterval(function() {MathJax.Hub.Typeset();}, 100);"))

Or you can add an .on("click") event on the button to typeset MathJax
expressions after, say, 100 milliseconds.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Help with... 'help'
parts:
Sorry I renamed the function from includeMathJax() to withMathJax() in
the development version. For static content, you only need to call
withMathJax() once, but for dynamic UI output, you have to call
withMathJax() every time you render new math expressions in the page.
Below is an example of popovers; note I used the option
`data-html`=true to make sure withMathJax() can typeset the math
expressions after the popover is rendered, and as the documentation of
Twitter Bootstrap has indicated, this may have potential security
problems: http://getbootstrap.com/2.3.2/javascript.html#popovers

helpPopup <- function(title, content,
placement=c('right', 'top', 'left', 'bottom'),
trigger=c('click', 'hover', 'focus', 'manual')) {
tagList(

tags$a(
href = "#", class = "btn btn-mini", `data-toggle` = "popover",
`data-html` = "true",

title = title, `data-content` = content, `data-animation` = TRUE,
`data-placement` = match.arg(placement, several.ok=TRUE)[1],
`data-trigger` = match.arg(trigger, several.ok=TRUE)[1],

tags$i(class="icon-question-sign")

),
tags$script("$(\"a[data-toggle='popover']\").popover();")
)
}

runApp(list(
ui = fluidPage(
h1('Math demo'),
withMathJax(helpText('static content $$\\sqrt{2}$$')),
helpText('more static content $$1-\\frac{1}{2}$$'),
uiOutput('foo')
),
server = function(input, output, session) {
output$foo = renderUI({
list(helpPopup("Test Math",withMathJax(HTML('math here $$\\alpha^2$$'))))
})
}
))


Regards,
Yihui

On Tue, Jul 2, 2013 at 2:23 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
Try slapping this at the top of ui.R:

helpPopup <- function(title, content,
                      placement=c('right', 'top', 'left', 'bottom'),
                      trigger=c('click', 'hover', 'focus', 'manual')) {
  tagList(
    singleton(
      tags$head(
        tags$script("$(\"[data-toggle='popover']\").popover()")
      )
    ),
    tags$a(
      href = "#", class = "btn btn-mini", `data-toggle` = "popover",
      title = title, `data-content` = content, `data-animation` = TRUE,
      `data-placement` = match.arg(placement, several.ok=TRUE)[1],
      `data-trigger` = match.arg(trigger, several.ok=TRUE)[1],
      
      tags$i(class="icon-question-sign")
    )
  )
}

Then sprinkle helpPopup calls liberally throughout your app :)

Greetings shiners,

Right now my app is nearly complete, but I noticed it is devoid of 'help' functionality.  Initially I suggested to a colleague that I have a checkbox for 'show instructions' to go along with each tab, displaying text in the main panel for telling the user what to do in each section.  However, she had an interesting idea, but I am not sure if it is beyond the capabilities of shiny at the moment or not.  She suggested that there be a help icon '?', which when moused over, would show the instructions for each section.  Currently, it appears that the mouse over text is simply the name of the tab which is currently selected, wherever it currently is.  Any suggestions on how to accomplish this, or other ways to supply help/instructions in an aesthetically pleasing manner, would all be very much appreciated.

Thanks,
Mike
